newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Iraqi mines have killed 1,700 in Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi mines have killed 1,700 in Kuwait.

text.p: Land mines planted in Kuwait during Iraq's 1990-91 occupation have killed about 1,700 civilians and injured 2,300, most of them children, an aid official was quoted as saying on Monday.

"The victims of mines in Kuwait amounted to 4,000 civilians of whom 1,700 died," al-Watan newspaper quoted Barjas al-Barjas, chairman of the Gulf state's Red Crescent Society, as saying. "The number of injured people was 2,300."
About 70 percent of people injured in mine explosions were children, he added. Exploding mines also killed 84 mine experts while another 200 were injured.
About five million anti-personnel mines were planted in Kuwait during the seven-month Iraqi occupation. Some 1,079 million mines were removed by the end of 1996, Barjas said.
Officials were not available for immediate comment.
Experts say sands shifted by wind make it hard to ensure any area is safe despite intense mine clearing efforts since the 1991 Gulf War that ended Iraq's occupation.
